title: Looking for recommendations in a unity workflow
author: Arouses
selftext:
Hey guys! Working on a dark fantasy builder and extraction isometric game within Unity. Primarily working with Astra/ Sol 6.1, but open to switching to Claude since I’m seeing some real good results with Opus 5.5, but worried about cost effectiveness. I’m a single dev and do have basic coding knowledge and pretty solid graphical design and modeling knowledge.

What workflows and tools/ MCP/ agents have you found to be the most helpful in creating high end assets and mechanics? 

My game is primarily fixed camera isometric with a zoom. Mostly high detailed pixel environments is my aim, kinda like if you mixed Octopath traveler and its use of modern lighting and effects pipelines with a dark fantasy and combat of Diablo. 

Any resources, tools, suggestions would be fantastic. Thank you so much.

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body:
Have the AI interrogate you about what your game is to be.


Have the AI build a workflow to track your work.


Have the AI build an asset pipeline for you get assets into your game.


Don't let the AI build bespoke tooling for things that exist. For example point to the unity blog post about how to profile instead of having the AI write log messages and parse it.


Good luck, have fun.

replies.author: Arouses
replies.body: Thank you for the suggestions! Mind I ask what you mean by the last part you wrote? I’m not sure I understand what you mean. Thanks!

replies.author: Seven-Prime
replies.body:
Sure.

So it will do what it can to figure something out. Then you'll be like, "Are you sure, why don't you use this?" And it'll be like, "Oh yeah that's way better."

Folks think you just pass stuff to ai and then you done. But you still need to know how to have a conversation about what you are doing or at least be aware of it. In the example I noticed that when the AI was doing performance testing, it was writing out log messages like, "Scene loaded in 2s. memory at 3%." And I have enough experience to know that is not how you profile code. By pointing the AI at the profiling best practices, the AI didn't have to write a bunch of code and instead just used the existing tools.

Basically, AI doesn't know everything. You still need to guide it. You act as a project manager working with a teammate. Challenge what it says and have it challenge what you say.

Also be prepared to read a lot of what it writes, and for your benefit, ask it to clarify things you don't understand enough.

comments.author: Novel-Thing880
comments.body: Octopath's look is mostly the lighting pass, so get Unity's 2D lights and bloom going first. My tileset painting stalled until I had concept plates to copy, and Mage Space makes dark fantasy mood plates from a prompt. Redraw them at tile size yourself, generated pixels never grid align.
